records.question: How much will my Apex plan pay per day towards the hospital room?
records.answer: Your Apex plan will pay up to **Rs. 7,500 per day** for the hospital room. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: Is there a daily cap on intensive care charges in the Apex plan?
records.answer: No. The policy states that ICU/ICCU charges have no sub‑limit – the insurer covers the actual charges up to the sum insured, so there is no daily cap on intensive care charges. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: For how many days before admission does the Apex plan cover my medical expenses?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield plan covers pre‑hospitalisation medical expenses for up to **60 days prior to admission** (linked to the illness)[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: What is the most the Apex plan pays for an ambulance each time I am hospitalised?
records.answer: The Apex plan covers up to **Rs. 3,500 per hospitalisation** for road ambulance charges. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How much does the Apex plan pay for Ayurveda and other AYUSH treatment?
records.answer: The Apex plan covers AYUSH (Ayurveda and other AYUSH) treatment up to **100 % of the Sum Insured** (subject to the linked‑to‑illness condition)[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: Does the Apex plan put a limit on day care procedures?
records.answer: Yes. The Apex Health Shield (v2) covers day‑care procedures up to the Sum Insured, but only for the first 30 days of coverage. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How long must I wait before the Apex plan pays for an illness that is not an accident?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield plan has an initial waiting period of **30 days** for all illnesses that are not accidental bodily injuries. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How many months do I have to wait for cataract surgery to be covered on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must wait **12 months** for cataract surgery to be covered under the Apex plan. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: When can I claim for hernia or piles treatment on the Apex plan?
records.answer:
You can claim for hernia or piles treatment only after the specific waiting period has elapsed.  
- For these conditions the policy requires a **24‑month waiting period** from the date of policy inception [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  
- If the condition is declared as a pre‑existing disease at the time the policy is taken, the waiting period extends to **36 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: After how long does the Apex plan cover a joint replacement?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield plan covers joint replacement surgery after a waiting period of **24 months** (unless the surgery is accidental)[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: How long is the wait for conditions I already had when I bought the Apex plan?
records.answer: For conditions you already had when you purchased the Apex Health Shield plan, the waiting period is 36 months from the date of inception. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: What is the most the Apex plan pays per eye for cataract surgery?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) plan pays up to **Rs. 60,000 per eye** for cataract surgery. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How often can I get a free annual health check-up on the Silver wellness plan?
records.answer: You can receive a free annual health check‑up once per year on the Harbor Wellness Silver plan. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: What is the biggest renewal discount I can earn through steps on the Gold wellness plan?
records.answer: The Gold wellness plan offers a maximum renewal discount of **up to 20 %** based on the number of steps you take. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: How much worldwide emergency cover does the Gold wellness plan give?
records.answer: The Harbor Wellness Gold plan includes worldwide emergency cover up to $50,000 [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: What is the daily limit on ICU charges under the Harbor wellness plan?
records.answer: There is no daily limit on ICU charges under the Harbor Wellness plan. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: How much air ambulance cover does the Gold wellness plan include?
records.answer: The Gold wellness plan includes air ambulance cover up to Rs. 5 Lakhs. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: How much does the critical illness rider pay out if I am diagnosed with cancer?
records.answer: The Critical Illness Rider pays **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** if you are diagnosed with “Cancer of Specified Severity”[SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: How many days must I survive after a heart attack to claim under the critical illness rider?
records.answer: You must survive **30 days** after a heart attack to be eligible to claim under the critical illness rider. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What does the critical illness rider pay for kidney failure needing dialysis?
records.answer: The critical illness rider pays **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for kidney failure requiring dialysis. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What commission does an agent in the Silver tier earn?
records.answer: An agent in the Silver tier earns a 7% commission. [AGENT_GUIDE_FAKE p.1]

records.question: How far back does the Apex plan look when deciding if a condition was pre-existing?
records.answer: The Apex plan considers a condition pre‑existing if it was present, diagnosed, or treated within **36 months prior to policy inception**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: How many days do I have to cancel the Apex plan and get my premium back after buying it?
records.answer: You have 15 days from the date you receive the policy schedule to cancel the Apex plan and receive a refund of your premium (subject to minimal administrative charges) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: Will the Apex plan pay for cosmetic surgery?
records.answer: No. Cosmetic surgery is excluded from coverage unless it is reconstructive surgery required after an accidental bodily injury. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Does the Apex plan pay if someone deliberately injures themselves?
records.answer: No. Claims arising from intentional self‑inflicted injury, suicide attempts, or hazardous adventure sports are strictly non‑payable under the Apex Health Shield policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: How much does the Apex plan pay for maternity?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) covers inpatient medical expenses for maternity (normal or cesarean delivery) up to **Rs. 50,000 per delivery** (after a 24‑month waiting period, for up to two deliveries)[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

records.question: Is surgery for weight loss covered by the Apex plan?
records.answer: No.  Weight‑loss surgery (bariatric surgery) is excluded from coverage under the Apex Health Shield (v2) policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: How early must I tell the insurer before a planned hospital stay on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must notify the insurer at least **48 hours before** a planned admission at a network hospital. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: How soon must I report an emergency admission on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must provide notice of an emergency admission within 24 hours of the emergency hospitalisation or before discharge, whichever comes first. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: How long after I leave hospital do I have to send in my claim papers on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must submit all required claim documents within **30 days of discharge** from the hospital. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: Do older customers pay part of the bill themselves on the Apex plan?
records.answer: Yes. Under Version 2 of the Apex Health Shield, insured persons aged 65 years and above are required to pay a mandatory co‑payment of 10 % of each admissible claim. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: How much does my cover grow each year I make no claim on the Apex plan?
records.answer:
Your cover increases by **20 % of the base Sum Insured for each claim‑free policy year**.  
This 20 % uplift is cumulative, but it stops once the total bonus reaches **100 % of the original base Sum Insured**.  

[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: What is the ceiling on the no-claim growth in cover on the Apex plan?
records.answer: The maximum cumulative bonus for no‑claim growth on the Apex plan is **100 % of the base Sum Insured** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: Does the Harbor wellness plan make senior citizens pay a share of the bill?
records.answer: I do not have enough information in the provided policy documents to answer this question.

records.question: How do I cancel the Harbor wellness plan after buying it, within the free-look window?
records.answer:
To cancel the Harbor Wellness Advantage plan within the free‑look period, simply send a written notice of cancellation to Harbor Mutual Insurance. The free‑look window is 15 days from the date the policy is delivered, so you must submit the written notice within that 15‑day period.  

[HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.4]

records.question: How long is the initial waiting period on the critical illness rider?
records.answer: The initial waiting period on the Critical Illness Rider is 90 days from the date of inception. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.2]

records.question: On the Apex plan, how long must I stay in hospital for it to count as inpatient treatment, and what is the daily room limit?
records.answer:
The policy defines inpatient hospitalisation as an admission that lasts at least **24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
The daily room rent allowance for a single private AC room is **Rs. 7,500 per day** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How does the Apex plan's definition of a pre-existing condition line up with the waiting period for such conditions?
records.answer:
The Apex plan defines a pre‑existing disease (PED) as any condition for which the insured had signs, symptoms, a diagnosis, or treatment within **36 months prior to policy inception** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
The waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception is also **36 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]. Thus, the definition’s time frame matches the waiting period applied to such conditions.

records.question: What waiting period and money limit does the Apex plan set for cataract surgery?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) sets a **12‑month waiting period** for cataract surgery and a **sub‑limit of Rs. 60,000 per eye**. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How does the maternity waiting period on the Apex plan compare with its general initial waiting period?
records.answer: I do not have enough information in the provided policy documents to answer this question.

records.question: What does the critical illness rider pay for a major organ transplant, and what extra donor cost does its endorsement add?
records.answer:
The Critical Illness Rider pays **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for a major organ (or bone‑marrow) transplant, with a survival period of 30 days [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].  

The special endorsement adds an **extra Rs 1,50,000** to cover inpatient donor‑harvesting medical expenses [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.3].

records.question: Did the daily room rent limit on the Apex plan go up or down between the older and newer version?
records.answer:
The daily room‑rent limit increased from the older version to the newer version.  
In the older version the sub‑limit was Rs. 5,000 per day [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2], whereas in the newer version it was raised to Rs. 7,500 per day [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How did the number of days of pre-hospital cover change between the old and new Apex plan?
records.answer:
The pre‑hospitalisation cover was extended from **30 days prior to admission** in the old Apex plan (v1) to **60 days prior to admission** in the new Apex plan (v2), an increase of **30 days**.  

- Old plan: 30 days prior to admission [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2]  
- New plan: 60 days prior to admission [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How did the cataract waiting period change between the old and new Apex plan?
records.answer: The cataract waiting period was shortened from 24 months in the old Apex plan (Version 1) to 12 months in the new Apex plan (Version 2) [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: Which version of the Apex plan has the shorter wait for conditions declared at purchase?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) has the shorter waiting period for conditions declared at purchase. It requires a 36‑month waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception, whereas the Critical Illness Rider (v1) requires a 48‑month waiting period for pre‑existing critical conditions [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.2] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: How did the co-payment for senior citizens change between the two Apex versions?
records.answer:
The mandatory co‑payment for insured persons aged 65 years and older was **20 %** under Apex Health Shield Version 1, and it was **reduced to 10 %** under Version 2.  
[APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.6] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]
